# Otto — OLT support agent

## Escalation notifications

Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,
`api.escalationWebhookSecretName` names a Secret with the keys `url` and,
optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

# Human access to the support agent's GCP projects

Repository: `re-cinq/Otto`, private. The file that declares who may read a
customer's conversation is `infra/terraform/access/main.tf`; this page explains
it. Cite both at one commit.

The api's logs land in Cloud Logging, so whoever can read the project's logs can
read what a customer typed. This page and the terraform root hold work email
addresses, role names and a one-line reason per person, and nothing else.

yet. Until it is, the only member is `user:placeholder@example.com`, and no

## Why

Escalation is a stated product requirement, not a fallback. Kristian's target and anti-target are both explicit: an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him, versus a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it - and the intended destination is a phone call, with OLT contacting the customer as soon as the agent can't answer. Nothing in either meeting says *where* an escalation lands, and OLT has no support platform today. `051` already put a hand-off sentence in the prompt with a guarded placeholder channel, `049` made TMS `unavailable`/`timeout` results branchable specifically for this issue, and `003` lists the hand-off as an unmapped destination. ## Escalation notifications

Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,
`api.escalationWebhookSecretName` names a Secret with the keys `url` and,
optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

## Why

With no escalation destination configured, nobody is notified. The escalation spec's first paragraph and FR-015 say so: the record stays at `no_destination_configured`. The re:cinq test environment runs exactly that way, because `deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml` sets no `escalationWebhookSecretName` while KU-14 is open.
